3D Printing in SA

By: Jo Munnik | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we look at 3D printing and the remarkable products that are being produced here in SA, from a chocolate factory to robo hands.

Summary:
3 D PRINTING IS REVOLUTIONIZING THE WORLD OF DESIGN & INVENTION AND A GREAT DEAL OF IT IS HAPPENING IN SOUTH AFRICA. FROM A 3-D PRINTED CHOCOLATE FACTORY, TO LAWN MOWERS AND EVEN ROBO HANDS.

HANS FOUCHE IS AN INVENTOR AND CHOCOLATIER. HE RUNS A 3D PRINTING FACTORY AND A CHOCOLATE SHOP, ALL THE CHOCOLATE MAKING MACHINES ARE 3D PRINTED. HE HAS MOST RECENTLY CREATED A 3-D PRINT OF A LAWN MOWER AND A VACUUM CLEANER, WHICH WORKS VERY WELL! FOR A FRACTION OF THE TIME AND COST.

RICHARD VAN AS USED 3-D PRINTING TO CREATE MECHANICAL HANDS, FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE MISSING HANDS OR FINGERS. RICHARD CUT OFF HIS FINGER SEVERAL YEARS AGO AND CREATED A MECHANICAL FINGER USING 3D PRINTING. HE THEN DEVELOPED THE ROBO HAND AND HAS PROVIDED OVER 800 CHILDREN IN SA WITH HANDS. HIS FOCUS IS NOW ON ASSISTING AMPUTEES WITH PROVIDING THEM WIHT NEW LIMBS. HE HAS DONE WORK IN SYRIA AND SUDAN AND PLANS TO GO TO ANGOLA SOON TOO.


Further information:
NARRATIVE ELEMENTS

3 D printing taken off globally .

What is being done her is SA - from printing a chocolates to lawn mowers, to a vacuum cleaner, to robo finger and robo hand. (Lots of visuals of these products, how they are made etc).

Speak to Hans Fourie.

Focus on Robo Hand with Richard & Waldo: How Robohand started (Richard lost his fingers and invented Robo Finger) , has helped over 800 children in SA like Waldo by making them mechanical hands, the process time etc of making mechanical hands, but the focus is now on

making mechanical hands for amputees in Syria, Sudan and next Angola. (HAVE FOOTAGE OF RICHARD WITH AMPUTEES IN SYRIA AND WITH DANIEL IN SUDAN)

Hope for IV with an amputee from Syria / Sudan. (TBC. Has been requested).

Are these prosthetics accepted as good and suitable by the medical world? Does anyone making them have a medical background? how do they compare to ordinary prosthetics – cost/how long the last/functionality - better or worse/ ?

3D printing also providing job opportunities as you literally can design and make anything - speak to Charlie who runs his little business making gadgets & laptop stands etc with Robo Beast printer. How it works etc.

The opportunities are limitless - need to bring in the magic here. See Bongani trying out these products.

When is the world is likely to change to all things 3D - are we likely to vacuum our houses with 3D vacuum cleaners instead of the ones we have now in the foreseeable future? Or mow our grass? How likely is it that we will be able to print our own 3D devices in the future - anything you can think of? I want a bicycle for example. "Oh, let me just go and print one!" Is that likely?

Can this be abused? Can they make things they shouldn’t be making like weapons etc who regulates what they make?

And is the stuff they make safe? The electronics? Will they blow up in your hand if they get too hot etc

Script:


(INTRO)

IN 2011 WE SHOWED YOU HOW 3D PRINTING TECHNOLOGY IS BEING USED TO PRODUCE HUMAN TISSUES AND REPLACEMENT ORGANS. NOW 3-D PRINTING IN SOUTH AFRICA IS BREAKING NEW GROUND WITH THE PRODUCTION OF MECHANICAL LIMBS.

MORTARS / EXPLOSIONS

SYRIA HAS BEEN IN THE GRIP OF A DEVASTATING WAR FOR THE PAST FOUR YEARS.
OVER 20 000 PEOPLE CAUGHT IN THE CONFLICT HAVE LOST THEIR LIMBS - INCLUDING CHILDREN.

RICHARD
THERE ARE PEOPLE WHO HAVE CUT BOTH ARMS OFF.
AND YOU MAKE AN ARM FOR SOMEONE AND THEY ARE HAVING A MEAL, WHERE THEY ARE FEEDING THEMSELVES.

VO
SOUTH AFRICAN JACK OF ALL TRADES, RICHARD VAN AS, HAS USED 3D PRINTING TO DEVELOP A COST EFFECTIVE AND TIME EFFICIENT ALTERNATIVE TO PROSTHETIC DEVICES. SETTING GLOBAL TRENDS.

HE IS TAKING HIS 3-D PRINTED ROBO HANDS ACROSS BORDERS TO SUDAN AND SYRIA WHERE HE HAS SET UP CLINICS THAT GIVE AMPUTEES NEW HOPE.

VO
BY TEACHING LOCALS THE CRAFT OF 3D PRINTING HE’S ENSURED THE CLINICS ARE SELF-SUSTAINABLE.

RICHARD
THERE IS ACTUALLY AMPUTEES MAKING HANDS FOR AMPUTEES, IN A WAR ZONE.

VO
THE PRINTER THAT HE DESIGNED, THE ROBO BEAST, HAS BEEN CREATED’ AND BUILT SPECIFICALLY FOR USE IN WAR TORN REGIONS.

RICHARD
ALL THESE MACHINES THAT WE TAKE TO THESE PLACES ARE SOLAR -POWERED AND BATTERY BACKED UP. AND THE REASON WE WANT THAT IS BECAUSE THERE IS NO INFRASTRUCTURE LEFT IN WAR ZONES. IT WAS DESIGNED WITH ALL THOSE THINGS I MIND.

VO
THE ROBO BEAST PRINTER COSTS UNDER R 40 000 AND MECHANICAL HANDS ARE JUST ONE OF MANY THINGS THAT IT CAN PRINT.

3D PRINTING HAS TAKEN THE WORLD OF TECHNOLOGY, INNOVATION AND DESIGN BY STORM.

THE USA HAS JUST LAUNCHED THE WORLD’S FIRST 3D PRINTED CAR, THE STRATI.

3D PRINTING IS IN ESSENCE THE PROCESS OF MAKING 3 DIMENSIONAL PHYSICAL OBJECTS FROM A DIGITAL DESIGN.

AND IT’S PRETTY SIMPLE- YOU CREATE A VIRTUAL DESIGN OF THE OBJECT IN MIND USING COMPUTER SOFTWARE.
THE PRINTER THEN MAKES THE OBJECT THROUGH ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING BY LAYING DOWN SUCCESSIVE LAYERS OF MATERIAL UNTIL THE ENTIRE OBJECT IS CREATED.

RICHARD I LIKE TO SAY, IF YOU CAN THINK IT SCRIPT IT YOU CAN PRINT IT
VO:
RICHARD’S JOURNEY INTO 3-D PRINTED MECHANICAL LIMBS STARTED FOR PERSONAL REASONS. IN 2011 HE SEVERED FOUR OF HIS FINGERS DURING A CARPENTRY ACCIDENT. GIVEN THE EXORBITANT COSTS OF PROSTHETICS, HE DECIDED TO SIMPLY PRINT HIMSELF NEW FINGERS.
RICHARD
AFTER THE INITIAL SHOCK, I DECIDED THAT I WAS GOING TO MAKE A SET OF FINGERS FOR MYSELF AS A REPLACEMENT.

BONGANI LINK
FROM JUST WANTING HIS FINGERS BACK, IT WAS RICHARD’S NEVER SAY DIE ATTITUDE THAT HAS PUT SOUTH AFRICA AT THE FOREFRONT OF EXCITING TECHNOLOGY.

RICHARD
BASICALLY I WAS CHALLENGED WHEN IT CAME TO MAKING A FULL HAND. A SOUTH AFRICAN LADY, SHE CONTACTED US. HER CHILD HAD AMNIOTIC BAND SYNDROME.

VO
RICHARD MET YOUNG LIAM DIPPENAAR IN 2012. HE HAS AMNIOTIC BAND SYNDROME,
A BIRTH DEFECT WHICH LEFT HIM WITHOUT A RIGHT HAND.

RICHARD

SHE REACHED OUT TO US AND SHE ASKED ME, CAN YOU MAKE A WHOLE HAND? AND I SAID, JA SURE.


VO
SINCE THEN HE HAS CHANGED THE LIVES OF OVER 800 PEOPLE BY PROVIDING THEM WITH ROBO HANDS AND ARMS.

WALDO IT WAS AN AMAZING EXPERIENCE.
BONGANI WHAT WAS AMAZING?
WALDO KNOWING YOU HAVE TWO HANDS – YOU CAN PICK A BALL UP WITH TWO HANDS
VO:
WALDO STEENKAMP WAS ALSO BORN WITH AMNIOTIC BAND SYNDROME; GIVEN THE COST OF A PROSTHETIC, IT WAS NOT AN OPTION FOR HIS PARENTS. BUT THIS ALL CHANGED IN 2013 WHEN HE BECAME ONE OF THE FIRST SOUTH AFRICANS TO RECEIVE A HOME GROWN 3-D PRINTED MECHANICAL HAND.


RICHARD:
…. WHEN THEY MOVE THEIR WRIST, THE FINGERS CLOSE… IT’S ANATOMICALLY DRIVEN.

VO:
PROSTHETIC LIMBS ARE INCREDIBLY EXPENSIVE AND RANGE BETWEEN R 30 000 AND R 400 000 MAKING THEM UNAFFORDABLE FOR MANY PEOPLE. A 3D PRINTED MECHANICAL HAND IS A FRACTION OF THE COST AND THE PRODUCTION PROCESS TAKES AN AVERAGE OF 10 HOURS. LIKE ALL PROSTHETICS, WEAR AND TEAR WILL SEE THE ROBO HAND NEED TO BE REPLACED OVER TIME.

RICHARD
TO PRINT A COMPLETE HAND, AN ADULT HAND, WORKS OUT TO ABOUT R 500.



RICHARD
THE BEST THING ABOUT 3D PRINTING, YOUR CHILD GROWS HE IS NOT GOING TO STAY THE SAME SIZE. SO BASICALLY YOU TAKE THE HARDWARE, YOU TRANSFER THAT TO THE NEXT HAND. AND THEN YOU JUST PRINT ANOTHER HAND.

BONGANI
DO YOU NEED TO HAVE A MEDICAL BACKGROUND TO BE ABLE TO DESIGN THESE DEVICES?

RICHARD
I AM OF THE OPINION, NO. WHAT WE HAVE SAID IS GET AN OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST TO HELP YOU.

VO: (IMAGES OF HANS’S FACTORY IN HIS GARAGE)
PART OF THE APPEAL OF 3D PRINTING IS THAT ANYONE CAN DO IT AND YOU LITERALLY CAN MAKE PRETTY MUCH ANYTHING - FROM MECHANICAL LIMBS TO CHOCOLATES.

HANS
FOR ME, THE MOST BEAUTIFUL ASPECT OF 3-D PRINTING IS THAT I CAN HAVE AN IDEA IN MY HEAD RIGHT NOW. AN HOUR LATER.. NOW I HAVE GOT IT HERE IN MY HAND. A REAL WORKING MODEL.

VO
HANS FOUCHE IS AN ENGINEER WHO USES 3D PRINTING TO RUN HIS CHOCOLATE FACTORY. FOR 19 YEARS HIS DECORATIONS HAVE MADE IT ONTO THE SHELVES OF SOME OF SA’S MOST POPULAR SUPERMARKETS.

HANS
A LOT OF PEOPLE HAVE EATEN CHOCOLATE CUPS AND CHOCOLATE DECORATIONS OF OURS AND THEY MOST PROBABLY DON’T KNOW THAT WAS ACTUALLY 3D PRINTED.

VO
HANS ALSO RUNS A 3D PRINTING WORKSHOP FROM HIS HOME WHERE HE RECENTLY PRINTED A LAWN MOWER AND VACUUM CLEANER. HE EVEN PRINTED THE 3D PRINTER HE USES. ON THE DAY WE VISITED HIM, HE SHOWED US HOW QUICK AND EASY IT IS TO PRINT A WHEEL FOR HIS LAWNMOWER.

BONGANI
AND HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO MAKE YOU A COMPLETE LAWNMOWER?

HANS
THAT COMPLETE LAWN MOWER HAVE TAKEN 9 HOURS AND THEN A FEW HOURS TO ASSEMBLE THE WHOLE THING. SO 9 HOURS.

BONGANI
AND IT COST YOU HOW MUCH?

HANS:
R 150 MATERIAL COSTS

BONGANI LINK
IT’S A VASE BY NIGHT AND A VACUUM CLEANER BY DAY. THIS IS HANS’S LATEST GADGET AND WHO KNOW IF IN THE FUTURE ALL HOUSEHOLDS WILL HAVE AN APPLIANCE JUST LIKE THIS.

BONGANI
CAN ANYONE DO THIS?

HANS
YES.

BONGANI
ARE WE IN THE FUTURE ARE WE GOING TO SEE PEOPLE NOT RUSHING OFF TO THEIR LOCAL RETAILER NOT TO BUY EXPENSIVE BRANDS. BUT ESSENTIALLY WILL RATHER BE MAKING THEIR OWN STUFF?


HANS
IT IS DEFINITELY POSSIBLE. … YES, YES YOU CAN DO IT.


BONGANI LINK
FROM LAWN MOWERS TO VACUUM CLEANERS TO MECHANICAL HANDS AND EVEN CHOCOLATE. THE SKY IS REALLY THE LIMIT WHEN IT COMES TO 3D PRINTING, IF YOU CAN THINK IT YOU CAN PRETTY MUCH MAKE IT.

VO
THE 3D DESIGNS OF THE ROBO HAND AND ARM ARE AVAILABLE FOR FREE ONLINE AND HAVE BEEN DOWNLOAD OVER 140 000 TIMES. RECENTLY A 7-YEAR CHILD FROM CHINA MADE HIS OWN MECHANICAL HAND USING THE SCHEMATICS.

RICHARD
THIS CHILD BUILT HIS OWN HAND. IT’S INCREDIBLE. HE’S GOT ONE HAND. HE BUILT THE HAND WITH HIS ONE HAND, NOW HE HAS TWO HANDS.

VO
WHEN IT COMES TO 3D PRINTING, THE OPPORTUNITIES ARE ENDLESS.

BONGANI
HANS, THE FUTURE IS HERE?

HANS
I CERTAINLY BELIEVE SO. YES, AND HERE IS THE PROOF. WE ARE GOING TO DO IT.

(END)





PROMOS


PROMO 1 - 15”
3D PRINTING IS CHANGING THE WORLD AS WE KNOW IT YOU CAN MAKE ANYTHING FROM MECHANICAL LIMBS TO LAWN MOWERS AND EVEN CHOCOLATE.
HANS: WE’VE REALLY GOT TO SAY, FORGET EVERYTHING YOU USED TO KNOW THIS IS FUTURE IS HERE.

PROMO 2 – 15”
OVER 20 000 PEOPLE HAVE LOST LIMBS DUE TO THE CONFLICT IN SYRIA.
THROUGH 3D PRINTING A SOUTH AFRICAN INVENTOR IS CHANGING THE LIVES OF HUNDREDS OF AMPUTEES.
RICHARD BYTE: YOU MAKE AN ARM FOR SOMEONE AND THEY ARE HAVING A MEAL, WHERE THEY ARE FEEDING THEMSELVES

PROMO 3 – 10”

A SOUTH AFRICAN INVENTOR IS SETTING GLOBAL TRENDS BY 3D PRINTING COST EFFECTIVE ALTERNATIVE TO PROSTHETICS. IF YOU CAN THINK IT SCRIPT IT YOU CAN PRINT IT

BONGANI LINK FROM JUST WANTING HIS FINGERS BACK, IT WAS RICHARD’S NEVER SAY DIE ATTITUDE THAT HAS PUT SOUTH AFRICA AT THE FOREFRONT OF EXCITING TECHNOLOGY. RICHARD BASICALLY I WAS CHALLENGED WHEN IT CAME TO MAKING A FULL HAND. A SOUTH AFRICAN LADY, SHE CONTACTED US. HER CHILD HAD AMNIOTIC BAND SYNDROME. VO RICHARD MET YOUNG LIAM DIPPENAAR IN 2012. HE HAS AMNIOTIC BAND SYNDROME, A BIRTH DEFECT WHICH LEFT HIM WITHOUT A RIGHT HAND. RICHARD SHE REACHED OUT TO US AND SHE ASKED ME, CAN YOU MAKE A WHOLE HAND? AND I SAID, JA SURE. VO SINCE THEN HE HAS CHANGED THE LIVES OF OVER 800 PEOPLE BY PROVIDING THEM WITH ROBO HANDS AND ARMS. WALDO IT WAS AN AMAZING EXPERIENCE. BONGANI WHAT WAS AMAZING? WALDO KNOWING YOU HAVE TWO HANDS – YOU CAN PICK A BALL UP WITH TWO HANDS VO: WALDO STEENKAMP WAS ALSO BORN WITH AMNIOTIC BAND SYNDROME; GIVEN THE COST OF A PROSTHETIC, IT WAS NOT AN OPTION FOR HIS PARENTS. BUT THIS ALL CHANGED IN 2013 WHEN HE BECAME ONE OF THE FIRST SOUTH AFRICANS TO RECEIVE A HOME GROWN 3-D PRINTED MECHANICAL HAND. RICHARD: …. WHEN THEY MOVE THEIR WRIST, THE FINGERS CLOSE… IT’S ANATOMICALLY DRIVEN. VO: PROSTHETIC LIMBS ARE INCREDIBLY EXPENSIVE AND RANGE BETWEEN R 30 000 AND R 400 000 MAKING THEM UNAFFORDABLE FOR MANY PEOPLE. A 3D PRINTED MECHANICAL HAND IS A FRACTION OF THE COST AND THE PRODUCTION PROCESS TAKES AN AVERAGE OF 10 HOURS. LIKE ALL PROSTHETICS, WEAR AND TEAR WILL SEE THE ROBO HAND NEED TO BE REPLACED OVER TIME. RICHARD TO PRINT A COMPLETE HAND, AN ADULT HAND, WORKS OUT TO ABOUT R 500. RICHARD THE BEST THING ABOUT 3D PRINTING, YOUR CHILD GROWS HE IS NOT GOING TO STAY THE SAME SIZE. SO BASICALLY YOU TAKE THE HARDWARE, YOU TRANSFER THAT TO THE NEXT HAND. AND THEN YOU JUST PRINT ANOTHER HAND. BONGANI DO YOU NEED TO HAVE A MEDICAL BACKGROUND TO BE ABLE TO DESIGN THESE DEVICES? RICHARD I AM OF THE OPINION, NO. WHAT WE HAVE SAID IS GET AN OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST TO HELP YOU. VO: (IMAGES OF HANS’S FACTORY IN HIS GARAGE) PART OF THE APPEAL OF 3D PRINTING IS THAT ANYONE CAN DO IT AND YOU LITERALLY CAN MAKE PRETTY MUCH ANYTHING - FROM MECHANICAL LIMBS TO CHOCOLATES. HANS FOR ME, THE MOST BEAUTIFUL ASPECT OF 3-D PRINTING IS THAT I CAN HAVE AN IDEA IN MY HEAD RIGHT NOW. AN HOUR LATER.. NOW I HAVE GOT IT HERE IN MY HAND. A REAL WORKING MODEL. VO HANS FOUCHE IS AN ENGINEER WHO USES 3D PRINTING TO RUN HIS CHOCOLATE FACTORY. FOR 19 YEARS HIS DECORATIONS HAVE MADE IT ONTO THE SHELVES OF SOME OF SA’S MOST POPULAR SUPERMARKETS. HANS A LOT OF PEOPLE HAVE EATEN CHOCOLATE CUPS AND CHOCOLATE DECORATIONS OF OURS AND THEY MOST PROBABLY DON’T KNOW THAT WAS ACTUALLY 3D PRINTED. VO HANS ALSO RUNS A 3D PRINTING WORKSHOP FROM HIS HOME WHERE HE RECENTLY PRINTED A LAWN MOWER AND VACUUM CLEANER. HE EVEN PRINTED THE 3D PRINTER HE USES. ON THE DAY WE VISITED HIM, HE SHOWED US HOW QUICK AND EASY IT IS TO PRINT A WHEEL FOR HIS LAWNMOWER. BONGANI AND HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO MAKE YOU A COMPLETE LAWNMOWER? HANS THAT COMPLETE LAWN MOWER HAVE TAKEN 9 HOURS AND THEN A FEW HOURS TO ASSEMBLE THE WHOLE THING. SO 9 HOURS. BONGANI AND IT COST YOU HOW MUCH? HANS: R 150 MATERIAL COSTS BONGANI LINK IT’S A VASE BY NIGHT AND A VACUUM CLEANER BY DAY. THIS IS HANS’S LATEST GADGET AND WHO KNOW IF IN THE FUTURE ALL HOUSEHOLDS WILL HAVE AN APPLIANCE JUST LIKE THIS. BONGANI CAN ANYONE DO THIS? HANS YES. BONGANI ARE WE IN THE FUTURE ARE WE GOING TO SEE PEOPLE NOT RUSHING OFF TO THEIR LOCAL RETAILER NOT TO BUY EXPENSIVE BRANDS. BUT ESSENTIALLY WILL RATHER BE MAKING THEIR OWN STUFF? HANS IT IS DEFINITELY POSSIBLE. … YES, YES YOU CAN DO IT. BONGANI LINK FROM LAWN MOWERS TO VACUUM CLEANERS TO MECHANICAL HANDS AND EVEN CHOCOLATE. THE SKY IS REALLY THE LIMIT WHEN IT COMES TO 3D PRINTING, IF YOU CAN THINK IT YOU CAN PRETTY MUCH MAKE IT. VO THE 3D DESIGNS OF THE ROBO HAND AND ARM ARE AVAILABLE FOR FREE ONLINE AND HAVE BEEN DOWNLOAD OVER 140 000 TIMES. RECENTLY A 7-YEAR CHILD FROM CHINA MADE HIS OWN MECHANICAL HAND USING THE SCHEMATICS. RICHARD THIS CHILD BUILT HIS OWN HAND. IT’S INCREDIBLE. HE’S GOT ONE HAND. HE BUILT THE HAND WITH HIS ONE HAND, NOW HE HAS TWO HANDS. VO WHEN IT COMES TO 3D PRINTING, THE OPPORTUNITIES ARE ENDLESS. BONGANI HANS, THE FUTURE IS HERE? HANS I CERTAINLY BELIEVE SO. YES, AND HERE IS THE PROOF. WE ARE GOING TO DO IT. (END) PROMOS PROMO 1 - 15” 3D PRINTING IS CHANGING THE WORLD AS WE KNOW IT YOU CAN MAKE ANYTHING FROM MECHANICAL LIMBS TO LAWN MOWERS AND EVEN CHOCOLATE. HANS: WE’VE REALLY GOT TO SAY, FORGET EVERYTHING YOU USED TO KNOW THIS IS FUTURE IS HERE. PROMO 2 – 15” OVER 20 000 PEOPLE HAVE LOST LIMBS DUE TO THE CONFLICT IN SYRIA. THROUGH 3D PRINTING A SOUTH AFRICAN INVENTOR IS CHANGING THE LIVES OF HUNDREDS OF AMPUTEES. IF YOU CAN THINK IT SCRIPT IT YOU CAN PRINT IT

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): we look at 3D printing and the remarkable products that are being produced here in SA, from a chocolate factory to robo hands.
metadata.Summary: 3 D PRINTING IS REVOLUTIONIZING THE WORLD OF DESIGN & INVENTION AND A GREAT DEAL OF IT IS HAPPENING IN SOUTH AFRICA. FROM A 3-D PRINTED CHOCOLATE FACTORY, TO LAWN MOWERS AND EVEN ROBO HANDS. HANS FOUCHE IS AN INVENTOR AND CHOCOLATIER. HE RUNS A 3D PRINTING FACTORY AND A CHOCOLATE SHOP, ALL THE CHOCOLATE MAKING MACHINES ARE 3D PRINTED. HE HAS MOST RECENTLY CREATED A 3-D PRINT OF A LAWN MOWER AND A VACUUM CLEANER, WHICH WORKS VERY WELL! FOR A FRACTION OF THE TIME AND COST. RICHARD VAN AS USED 3-D PRINTING TO CREATE MECHANICAL HANDS, FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE MISSING HANDS OR FINGERS. RICHARD CUT OFF HIS FINGER SEVERAL YEARS AGO AND CREATED A MECHANICAL FINGER USING 3D PRINTING. HE THEN DEVELOPED THE ROBO HAND AND HAS PROVIDED OVER 800 CHILDREN IN SA WITH HANDS. HIS FOCUS IS NOW ON ASSISTING AMPUTEES WITH PROVIDING THEM WIHT NEW LIMBS. HE HAS DONE WORK IN SYRIA AND SUDAN AND PLANS TO GO TO ANGOLA SOON TOO.
metadata.Further information: NARRATIVE ELEMENTS 3 D printing taken off globally . What is being done her is SA - from printing a chocolates to lawn mowers, to a vacuum cleaner, to robo finger and robo hand. (Lots of visuals of these products, how they are made etc). Speak to Hans Fourie. Focus on Robo Hand with Richard & Waldo: How Robohand started (Richard lost his fingers and invented Robo Finger) , has helped over 800 children in SA like Waldo by making them mechanical hands, the process time etc of making mechanical hands, but the focus is now on making mechanical hands for amputees in Syria, Sudan and next Angola. (HAVE FOOTAGE OF RICHARD WITH AMPUTEES IN SYRIA AND WITH DANIEL IN SUDAN) Hope for IV with an amputee from Syria / Sudan. (TBC. Has been requested). Are these prosthetics accepted as good and suitable by the medical world? Does anyone making them have a medical background? how do they compare to ordinary prosthetics – cost/how long the last/functionality - better or worse/ ? 3D printing also providing job opportunities as you literally can design and make anything - speak to Charlie who runs his little business making gadgets & laptop stands etc with Robo Beast printer. How it works etc. The opportunities are limitless - need to bring in the magic here. See Bongani trying out these products. When is the world is likely to change to all things 3D - are we likely to vacuum our houses with 3D vacuum cleaners instead of the ones we have now in the foreseeable future? Or mow our grass? How likely is it that we will be able to print our own 3D devices in the future - anything you can think of? I want a bicycle for example. "Oh, let me just go and print one!" Is that likely? Can this be abused? Can they make things they shouldn’t be making like weapons etc who regulates what they make? And is the stuff they make safe? The electronics? Will they blow up in your hand if they get too hot etc
